subject: Evaluation quickstart & environment bridging — credential handoff and timeline
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@mediscan.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation quickstart & environment bridging — credential handoff and timeline

Hi Alyssa,

Great speaking earlier — appreciate the clarity on Mediscan's evaluation objectives. To keep momentum I sketched a short 'quickstart' MAP that covers the environment pieces we discussed: org setup, API key provisioning, IP allowlist, and optional VPC peering. Goal: get a small staging workload running within 10 business days so your infra team can run throughput and latency checks.

High-level steps (proposed timeline):
- Day 0–1: Exchange onboarding docs & select evaluation cluster region (us-west-2)
- Day 1–2: Create Mediscan org in Redwood Console + invite initial users (security lead + dev lead)
- Day 2–3: Generate API keys (scoped) and provide api-key-template.txt for secure rotation
- Day 3–6: IP allowlist entries added (we'll provide CIDR for our egress and staging nodes)
- Day 5–8: Optional VPC peering request (if you want private network path) — dependency on your NetOps window
- Day 8–10: Smoke tests, sample workload run, and short sync to review results

Attachments: MAP_v1_Redwood-Mediscan.pdf (draft MAP), network-handshake-diagram.png (illustrative).

Could you confirm: 1) who from Mediscan will be the technical point of contact for keys and peering? 2) any blackout windows for peering requests this month? If you prefer, we can turn this into a mutual action plan with checkpoints inside HubSpot.

Thanks — I can loop in Aditya if you'd like a runbook for the VPC peering steps.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Evaluation quickstart & environment bridging — credential handoff and timeline

Thanks Ben — this looks good and pragmatic. Quick answers:
- Technical POC: Harry Bennett (cc'd) will own keys/peering and coordinate with our NetOps.
- Peering blackout: we have a maintenance window Jul 4–5; prefer to avoid peering changes then.
- We prefer API keys scoped to a staging org and rotation docs.

A few clarifying Qs before we commit to the 10-day plan:
1) For IP allowlist, can you provide both single-IP and CIDR suggestions? Our NetOps prefers small CIDR blocks for staging.
2) If we don't do VPC peering in the first wave, can we still run representative latency tests over the public ingress?

Harry — I'll hand to you for technical alignment, but Ben/Marissa please keep me in the loop on the MAP doc updates.

- Alyssa
Alyssa Turner

Hi Alyssa / Ben — tagging in Aditya for the peering/runbook details. Answers inline and a short checklist we can run as the MAP's operational steps.

Answers:
- IP formats: we'll send both a /32 and a /27 suggestion for staging traffic. If your NetOps prefers minimal surface we can keep to the /32s for the test nodes.
- Latency tests over public ingress: yes — representative but expect ~8–15ms variation compared to peering; we always call out that private peering reduces variability for tail latency.

Quick operational checklist (for MAP task items):
1) Redwood: create Mediscan org + create two scoped API keys (staging-read, staging-infer) — deliver encrypted via your secure channel.
2) Mediscan: add listed CIDRs to staging allowlist and confirm egress NAT ranges for any reverse-proxy.
3) Mediscan Ops: schedule peering request (if doing now) outside Jul 4–5 window; provide VPC IDs & account numbers.
4) Redwood/Mediscan: run smoke test job (we provide sample traffic harness) and capture token usage & P99 latencies.
5) Sync: 30-minute call to review results and decide on next steps (canary workload vs expanded traffic).

Attachments included: api-key-template.txt (small template with rotation instructions).

Proposed next sync: Fri Jul 6, 10:00 PT — does that work for you Harry?

Thanks,
Marissa
Delivery Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
